name: Claude Code
shortDescription: Anthropic's agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files and runs commands from the terminal, IDE, desktop app or browser.
description:
Claude Code is an agentic coding tool from Anthropic. According to its documentation, it reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands and integrates with your development tools, and it is available in the terminal, in IDE extensions, in a desktop app and in the browser.

It is built to work across multiple files rather than complete single lines. You describe a feature, a bug or an automation task, and it works through the project to carry it out. Installation is a single command on macOS, Linux and Windows, and VS Code and JetBrains integrations are offered. Most surfaces need a Claude subscription or an Anthropic Console account, and the terminal CLI, VS Code and JetBrains also support third-party providers.

On Anthropic's pricing page, Claude Code is included in the paid individual plans (Pro and Max) and is not included in the Free plan. Team plans list Claude Code on their premium seat, and Enterprise is priced as a per-seat fee plus usage at API rates. Each plan has usage limits, so heavy daily use is the main reason people move up from Pro to Max.

The main trade-off is that it is a subscription or metered product tied to Anthropic's models, and it expects you to be comfortable reviewing code changes it makes in your repository.
bestFor: Developers who want an AI agent that works across a whole codebase from the terminal or IDE, and are comfortable reviewing the changes it makes
notFor: People who want a free tool (Claude Code is not in the Free plan) or who only need inline autocomplete rather than an agent

verdict: Claude Code is a strong choice for developers who want an agent that works across a whole repository rather than an autocomplete tool. It is not free and usage limits apply, so try it on Pro and move up only if you hit the limits. Skip it if you want inline suggestions only or cannot review the changes it makes.

name: DeepSeek
shortDescription: AI lab offering a chat app and a pay-as-you-go API with 1M-token context and OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints.
description:
DeepSeek is an AI company whose models are available through a web chat, a mobile app and a developer API platform. Its homepage highlights the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash release and offers deep thinking and search modes in the chat interface.

For developers, the API documentation lists two models: deepseek-flash (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) and deepseek-v4-pro. Both support a 1M-token context length, JSON output, tool calls, a Responses API and an Anthropic-format API, and thinking and non-thinking modes. Flash also supports vision, while Pro does not. The API is reachable in OpenAI format and in Anthropic format, which makes it easy to point existing clients and coding tools at it.

Pricing is usage-based and quoted per 1M tokens, with separate rates for cache hits, cache misses and output, and with lower off-peak rates that are half of the peak rates. Peak hours are 01:00 to 04:00 and 06:00 to 10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. Search and Fetch are billed per 1,000 successful requests.

The documentation also warns that prices may vary and that DeepSeek reserves the right to adjust them. This page covers the API pricing published by DeepSeek; it does not state a price for the consumer chat app.
bestFor: Developers who want a low-cost, usage-based API with a very long context window and OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoints
notFor: Teams that need fixed monthly pricing, or that have data-residency or vendor-location requirements they have not checked against DeepSeek's terms

name: Microsoft OneDrive
shortDescription: Microsoft's cloud storage service for syncing, sharing and backing up files, sold inside Microsoft 365 subscriptions for individuals.
description:
OneDrive is Microsoft's cloud storage service. Its plans page describes secure storage and ransomware protection for files and photos, with sync across PC, Mac, iPhone, iPad and Android phones and tablets. For individuals it is sold through Microsoft 365 plans that bundle storage with the Office apps.

On the individual plans page, Microsoft 365 Basic includes 100 GB of cloud storage for one person. Microsoft 365 Personal includes 1 TB, Family includes 2 TB shared by up to six people, and Premium includes up to 6 TB (1 TB per person) for up to six people. Personal, Family and Premium also include the Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote desktop apps with Microsoft Copilot features, with usage levels that differ by plan.

The key OneDrive features Microsoft lists include Personal Vault, real-time collaboration, easy file sharing with password-protected or expiring links, ransomware detection and file restore, Windows backup, version history, camera roll backup, offline files and advanced sync between PC, Mac and the cloud. Storage can be expanded up to 10 TB on the higher plans.

The plans page also has a Business tab and links to enterprise plans, which this entry does not cover. Because the storage is sold inside Microsoft 365 plans, OneDrive is best judged as part of that bundle rather than as a standalone storage price.
bestFor: People already using Windows or Microsoft 365 who want file sync and backup bundled with the Office apps
notFor: People who want a standalone storage plan without paying for a Microsoft 365 bundle, or who need business-specific features that this entry does not cover

verdict: OneDrive is the natural choice if you already live in Windows and the Office apps and want storage and backup included in the same subscription. If you only want a simple storage plan or have business needs, compare it against dedicated storage services first.
